source.title: Is network fragmentation a useful complexity measure?
source.authors: Coenraad Mouton; Randle Rabe; Daniël G. Haasbroek; Marthinus W. Theunissen; H. L. Potgieter; M. Davel

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether fragmentation measures track generalization error and gap rankings, using different measures from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study measures fragmentation across model capacities and evaluates fragmentation-based scores against generalization gaps. It does not test the specific interventions or settings named in V1–V8. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study's own width sweep bears on V2 in a new architecture: four-layer CNNs on CIFAR-10. Section A.2 states that clean models with k > 9 and corrupted-label models with k > 11 reach zero training error, while Section 2 reports a second descent in test error. Fragmentation prediction alone would not test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that fragmentation-based measures show promise for predicting generalization, track held-out error in controlled double-descent experiments, and are not simply explained by large weight norms. They leave the underlying mechanism unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Measures classification-region fragmentation and its association with test error and generalization-gap rankings; does not test the interventions or measures in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Predictive performance varies with fragmentation metric and representation space; input-space measures perform better overall than hidden-space measures, with Task 1 an exception.

fits_no_version.finding: Fragmentation follows test error across capacity and validation error during training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Classification-region fragmentation tracks held-out error in these controlled CNN experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Input-space fragmentation measures predict PGDL generalization-gap rankings. Test CMI means are 17.01 for fragmentation, 25.90 for foreign-region coverage, and 25.94 for foreign-class coverage.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Classification-region coverage measures can rank CNN generalization gaps and outperform region counts on average.

fits_no_version.finding: Input-space measures outperform hidden-space measures on average. Depth effects are not uniformly decreasing: fragmentation's test mean rises from 0.16 at the first hidden layer to 0.24 at the last. Task 1 favors the last layer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The predictive performance of fragmentation measures depends on representation space and task.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight norms do not simply explain fragmentation, although shallow convolutional-layer mean absolute weights increase around its peak.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fragmentation is not explained solely by large parameter norms.

record.peer_reviewed: Workshop on Scientific Methods for Understanding Deep Learning, NeurIPS 2024
record.problems: The controlled double-descent curves are presented as figures without numerical values in the text. PGDL scores summarize tasks and do not provide uncertainty estimates. The fragmentation measurements use 500 sampled triplets.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 task-specific values for fragmentation, FRC, FCC and comparator measures were omitted; aggregate development and test means were retained. Table 2 task-specific values were omitted; test-set means were retained. Figure-only capacity and training curves are represented by R1–R3.

untested.parts: No paired experiment fitting fully random labels and natural labels with the same architecture and recipe, including held-out chance performance.

The original one-hidden-layer networks and datasets are not replicated. Training uses fixed 500-epoch budgets rather than demonstrated convergence; exact test-error changes and monotonicity at every width cannot be read from the supplied figures.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
Adam is used, but optimizers and tuning budgets are not compared.
Batch size is fixed at 256; no batch-size comparison.
No magnitude-scaled weight perturbation measure or comparison of its gap rankings against norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal and retraining experiment based on example memorization.

record.verdict_notes: The extraction excludes V2 too narrowly based on architecture. Its width and train/test-error results test the same question in a new CNN setting. R4–R15 are evaluations of the study's proposed measures and should remain outside evidence for V1–V8. Qualitative V2 verdicts rely on explicit textual descriptions; exact curve values are unavailable.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train the same architectures and recipes on fixed random labels and natural labels.
Uses four-convolutional-layer CNNs on CIFAR10, not one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10; does not test the specified width claim.
Does not compare convolutional networks with fully connected networks.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or test optimizer tuning.
Measures fragmentation and its predictive performance, not magnitude-aware sharpness or the specified norm- and margin-based comparisons.
Does not remove memorized examples or compare retraining after removing them with random-example removal.

rows.subject: CNN models, clean CIFAR10; mean over three seeds
rows.size_stated: 4 convolutional layers with [k, 2k, 4k, 8k] channels, k between 4 and 64; dense layer of 400 nodes
rows.operation_detail: Measured input-space fragmentation against test error across model capacity.
rows.note: Text says the mean fragmentation curve closely follows the test-error curve; exact values are only shown in figures.
rows.check: The test-error component bears on V2; fragmentation itself does not. The text establishes the qualitative second descent despite unavailable numerical curve values. Record zero training error for k > 9 and compare wider models with narrower interpolating models.

conditions.value: CIFAR10; 10% of training labels randomly assigned a different label

rows.note: Text says the label-corrupted models show pronounced double descent and generally higher mean fragmentation than clean models.
rows.check: The test-error component bears on V2; fragmentation itself does not. The authors explicitly report pronounced double descent. For V2 the relevant baseline is narrower interpolating models within the corrupted-label condition, rather than clean-data models. Zero training error occurs for k > 11.

relationships.condition: Clean CIFAR-10; four-convolutional-layer CNN width sweep, three seeds, 500 epochs.
relationships.reason: R1's test-error curve and Section 2 report a second descent; Section A.2 establishes zero training error for k > 9. This supports the post-interpolation width trend in this CNN setting.
relationships.display_finding: The reported second descent after zero training error on clean data remains unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 with 10% corrupted training labels; four-convolutional-layer CNN width sweep, three seeds, 500 epochs.
relationships.reason: R2 and Section 2 report pronounced double descent; Section A.2 establishes zero training error for k > 11. Test error falls again as width increases in the interpolating regime.
relationships.display_finding: The reported second descent after zero training error with corrupted labels remains unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
